children: Sweden industrial group Q3 net sales rose 13% yr/yr, slightly missing analyst expectations
Q3 EBITA rose 19% and slightly beat analyst expectations
Order intake grew 16% yr/yr, with strongest gains in medical, energy and engineering segments
Company says strong order backlog and acquisitions support outlook for coming quarters
Company notes ongoing economic uncertainty mainly due to geopolitical situation
Company says energy investments in Europe contribute to order backlog, with long project lead times
SEGMENT DEMAND - Co said order intake growth was strongest in medical technology, pharmaceuticals, energy and engineering segments
ACQUISITIONS - Acquisitions contributed 8% to net sales growth in the quarter
PRICING AND ORGANIC GROWTH - Margin improvement attributed to organic sales growth and successful pricing efforts
*Applies to a deviation of less than 1%; not applicable for per-share numbers.
The current average analyst rating on the shares is "buy" and the breakdown of recommendations is 5 "strong buy" or "buy", 3 "hold" and no "sell" or "strong sell"
The average consensus recommendation for the industrial machinery & equipment peer group is "buy"
Wall Street's median 12-month price target for Indutrade AB is SEK280.00, about 8.3% above its October 22 closing price of SEK258.60
The stock recently traded at 26 times the next 12-month earnings vs. a P/E of 23 three months ago
